title: Microprogress Canvas — weekly retro & experiments
content:
Purpose: quick, actionable weekly snapshot that combines metric signal, habit checkpoints, and one small experiment to run next week. Not a formal OKR doc — this is my lightweight cadence to prevent scope creep and maintain momentum.

Topline outcome (one sentence): Keep token-cost-per-feature under 0.85 of baseline while improving 1 user-facing latency percentiles via batching/timeout tuning test.

Context (why this matters):
- Dedicated capacity trial is next month; want a clean set of personal targets so I can handoff reliable numbers to infra and SRE.
- My common failure: chasing big refactors instead of small, measurable experiments. This canvas forces microprogress.

Weekly snapshot (2025-11-30 to 2025-12-06)
- Primary metric: user-facing p95 latency for chat route — baseline 420ms, target <= 395ms.
- Secondary metric: tokens/second cost-adjusted index — baseline 1.0, target <= 0.85.
- Habit check (daily): 20–30m focused time blocks for experiment work — hit 4/7 days.
- Energy signal: 6/10 average (notes: travel mid-week lowered throughput).

What I shipped this week (short bullets):
- Small batching config: reduced batch timeout from 8ms to 6ms on dev cluster A. Observed reduced average latency for short prompts.
- Promptset curation: trimmed 12 noisy prompts from monitoring set (old chatbot ext) — reduced eval noise.
- Retro writeup for last playtest with DS team (shared in Slack #playtests).

Results & observations (data-backed where possible):
- p95 latency: 412ms (–8ms vs baseline). p50 unchanged. p99 spikes remain (investigate long-tail).
- Cost index: 0.92 — improvement but not yet at 0.85. KV-cache hit rate increased by ~3% after prompt trimming.
- User impact: one customer reported improved responsiveness in early AM testing window.

Hypotheses for next week (ranked):
1) Reducing batch timeout further to 4ms will shave p95 by another ~10–12ms on short prompts without increasing cost significantly. (effort: 1 small config + perf run)
2) Introduce a tiny prefix cache for the three most common prompt prefixes — should improve cache hit by 6–8% on our workload (effort: 2–3 hours to prototype).
3) Tweak kernel selection preference for medium-length sequences on dev GPU to see if p99 allocation improves (effort: handoff to infra / collab).

Experiment plan (this week):
- Primary experiment: reduce batch timeout to 4ms on dev cluster B, run 24h A/B vs current 6ms. Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99, cost index, queue fill rate. (success criteria: p95 <= 395ms and cost index <= 0.88)
- Secondary experiment (if time): lightweight prefix cache in front of request router for top-3 prefixes — run 2h smoke tests then 12h sample.

Risks & failure modes (what I’ll watch):
- Lowering timeout might increase total GPU overhead per-token (counterproductive for cost). Monitor tokens/sec and cost index closely.
- Cache experiment could introduce subtle staleness for ephemeral user state — ensure prefix list excludes user-specific tokens.
- Infra flakiness: dev cluster B has had two reboots in last 10 days — coordinate with SRE before long runs.

Planned checkpoints / quick checklist:
- [ ] Create Linear task for batch-timeout A/B (link to LINEAR-2247).
- [ ] Add metric dashboard panel for cost-index (hourly granularity).
- [ ] Run 24h A/B and collect perf dump.
- [ ] Post result snapshot to #personal-experiments and tag Lina/Noah.

Personal process notes (meta):
- Use 2 Pomodoros (~50m) on Monday morning to get the A/B config set up when energy is high.
- Keep experiment small: only change one variable at a time. If time runs out, stop and document interim signal.
- Aim to keep writeups < 300 words when sharing results; include exact numbers and graphs link.

Retrospective prompts (for next week):
- Did the micro-experiment deliver directional improvement? If not, why?
- What was the easiest part of the week? The hardest?
- Did I accidentally scope creep? Which tasks bubbled up and why?

Personal development: skill focus for the sprint
- Learn more about kernel selection tradeoffs — set aside two 60m sessions with infra teammate.
- Practice concise experiment writeups (goal: 250 words max).

Loose notes / snippets to capture:
- Example metric formula for cost-index: (total compute cost / baseline compute cost) * (1 + penalty * cache-miss-rate). Need to formalize.
- Possible quick wins: trim largest 5% of longest prompts by length or route them to dedicated policy.
- Share experiment with Lina as a sanity check before long run.

Open questions:
- If p99 remains stubborn, do we prioritize kernel changes or routing (regional fallback)? Which yields less operational risk?
- What is the acceptable short-term cost delta for a 10–15ms improvement in p95? (talk to product for SLO tradeoff)

Action items (next 7 days):
- Monday: create Linear task, update dashboard, set up A/B config (2 Pomodoros).
- Tuesday: start A/B run, post initial note (end of day).
- Thursday: check midpoint signals (12h), escalate to SRE if cluster reboots.
- Friday: compile results, short writeup, decide next action (scale, revert, or new hypothesis).

Final thoughts (one-liner to close): Keep experiments tiny, measurable, and shareable — momentum grows from many small wins, not one big refactor.

-- Arjun
